name: Refractory Cytopenia with Multilineage Dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: World Health Organization (WHO) 2016 Classification Criteria for Myelodysplastic Syndromes

criteria.description: Presence of persistent cytopenia in one or more hematopoietic lineages (anemia, neutropenia, or thrombocytopenia)
Dysplastic changes affecting ≥10% of cells in two or more myeloid cell lines in the bone marrow
Bone marrow blast percentage less than 20%
Exclusion of other causes of cytopenias and dysplasia such as vitamin deficiencies, infections, or other hematologic malignancies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Persistent cytopenia in at least one lineage, dysplasia in ≥10% of cells in two or more myeloid lineages, and bone marrow blasts <20%, with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires bone marrow examination and exclusion of secondary causes.

pathognomonic.notes: Reduction in red cells, white cells, and/or platelets
searchTerms: low blood counts in multiple cell types

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bone marrow dysplasia in multiple myeloid lineages
searchTerms: bone marrow producing defective blood cells
low red blood cells with low reticulocytes
persistent anemia with poor new cell production
frequent infections from low white cells
fatigue related to low red blood cells

rare.notes: Signs of progression to acute myeloid leukemia

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms secondary to anemia-induced hypoxia
searchTerms: brain symptoms from low oxygen due to anemia
cognitive problems from low blood oxygen

laboratory: Dysplastic features in peripheral blood smear
Bone marrow aspirate showing multilineage dysplasia
imaging: Occasional splenomegaly or hepatomegaly on ultrasound or CT
genetic: Somatic mutations in genes such as SF3B1, TET2, ASXL1, and RUNX1
Cytogenetic abnormalities including monosomy 7, del(5q), or complex karyotype
other: Exclusion of vitamin B12/folate deficiency and other secondary causes

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of ≥15% ring sideroblasts in bone marrow
Usually isolated anemia without multilineage dysplasia
More aggressive clinical course with systemic symptoms

redFlags: Rapidly increasing blast count in bone marrow
Severe pancytopenia with bleeding or infection
references: Arber DA, et al. The 2016 revision to the World Health Organization classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia. Blood. 2016.
Tefferi A, Vardiman JW. Myelodysplastic syndromes. N Engl J Med. 2009.
